entities.name: René of Anjou
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
René I of Anjou (1409–1480) emerged as a central, albeit often thwarted, figure in 15th-century European dynastic politics, inheriting and aggressively pursuing claims to multiple crowns and territories including the Duchy of Anjou, the Kingdom of Naples, the Kingdom of Jerusalem, and the Duchy of Lorraine. His life encapsulates the intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and succession disputes that characterized the late medieval period, particularly the struggle between the Houses of Anjou and Aragon for control of Southern Italy, and the broader context of the Hundred Years' War. Despite his repeated military failures, René's cultural patronage profoundly shaped the artistic and literary landscape of Provence, earning him the moniker "the Good King René."

Born into the House of Valois-Anjou, a cadet branch of the French royal family, René's early life was marked by the acquisition of Lorraine through marriage to Isabella, Duchess of Lorraine, in 1420. His most significant political endeavor was his claim to the Kingdom of Naples, which he inherited from his adoptive father Louis III of Anjou in 1434. He actively campaigned for the Neapolitan throne, reigning in Naples from 1435 until 1442, when he was decisively expelled by Alfonso V of Aragon after a protracted siege. He also held the title King of Sicily, King of Jerusalem, and King of Aragon (as counter-king), though these were largely titular. His later years were devoted to consolidating his Provençal territories and fostering a vibrant court culture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: René of Anjou, despite his political and military failures in consolidating his vast inherited claims, profoundly shaped the cultural landscape of Provence and influenced the artistic currents of the late medieval period. His legacy is more enduring in the arts than in the realm of statecraft, contributing to the distinct character of the 'Good King René' in French history.

entities.summary: René I of Anjou was Duke of Anjou and Count of Provence from 1434 to 1480, who also reigned as King of Naples from 1435 to 1442. Having spent his last years in Aix-en-Provence, he is known in France as the Good King René.
